name: Thoracic Myelopathy / Thoracic Spinal Cord Compression
definition: Spinal cord dysfunction caused by thoracic canal compromise from degenerative, ossific, neoplastic, infectious, vascular or other lesions.

typical: Sensory level or band-like trunk symptoms

redFlags.item: Acute weakness, fever/infection, cancer or trauma with cord symptoms

core: Cervical and lumbar screening for tandem disease

investigations.principle: Suspected thoracic myelopathy requires prompt cause-directed imaging.
investigations.MRI: Thoracic MRI is the key test; contrast when infection, tumour or inflammation is suspected.
investigations.radiographs: Radiographs are limited for cord assessment; CT better characterizes ossification/bony lesions.

green: Rehabilitation only after cord stability and treatment plan are established
amber: Do not use forceful spinal manipulation when unexplained cord compression is possible.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Individualized Vata-vyadhi neurological phenotype may be documented only in parallel with the modern cord-compression diagnosis.

patientEducation.summary: Spinal cord dysfunction caused by thoracic canal compromise from degenerative, ossific, neoplastic, infectious, vascular or other lesions.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for new/progressive major weakness, gait deterioration, bladder/bowel dysfunction, saddle sensory loss, fever/systemic illness with severe spinal/joint pain, major trauma, or other listed red flags.
